memory_update.text: The merged High-Tech Global Supply Chain Layer 1 universe should stay multi-vertical: AI photonics, advanced packaging/process control, semiconductor equipment subsystems, robotics precision motion, and aerospace/defense-qualified electronics.
AI photonics remains the strongest evidenced node in this pass, led by AXTI, VECO, SIVEF, POET, AAOI, AEHR, LITE, and COHR, but revenue purity and customer validation remain critical.
Advanced packaging and inspection/metrology should remain a separate node with CAMT, ONTO, NVMI, BESI.AS, and PDFS as candidates for later evidence validation.

Robotics precision motion should remain distinct from robot OEMs; candidates include harmonic reducers, actuators, motion control, machine vision, and sensor suppliers rather than humanoid brands alone.

Layer 1C has enough breadth for an initial dashboard universe but not enough primary-source validation; Layer 2 should verify filings, current market caps, revenue purity, customer links, and falsification triggers.

summary: Layer 1C merges the Layer 1A theme map and visible Layer 1B node-level candidates into a deduplicated Serenity-style initial universe for High-Tech Global Supply Chain bottleneck research. The universe is intentionally not a mega-cap AI list: reference leaders are included as architecture anchors, while the ranking favors underfollowed or niche public companies sitting in AI photonics inputs, compound semiconductor tools, advanced packaging/process control, robotics precision motion, and aerospace/defense-qualified electronics. Scores are Layer 1 research-priority scores only, not investment recommendations. Several candidates remain hypotheses because this pass has not yet validated current filings, segment revenue, customer concentration, market capitalization, or order conversion.
